prerequisites: The course has no specific requirements, although for proper monitoring and utilization, it is recommended that the student be familiar with fundamentals of mathematical calculus, mechanics, and materials science.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge applied to manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level which, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: Iron and steel production and casting
Machine tools with rotary cutting movement
Machine tools with rectilinear cutting movement
teaching_methods: Autonomous work (through proposed activities and virtual course tools like forums)
Reading guidelines available on the virtual course
Study of topics through basic and complementary bibliography
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained from a 90% written theoretical/practical exam, a 5% voluntary online Continuous Assessment Test (PEC), and 5% laboratory practicals. To pass the course, attendance at practicals is mandatory. The PEC only contributes positively if the written exam is passed in the ordinary call, and a minimum of 5 out of 10 is required in the exam to sum the PEC. For the September resit, practicals can only be attended if the exam has been passed. If the course is not passed, the practicals completed are validated for subsequent academic years.
